text: Dev-only flag to skip server TLS cert validation (forced off in release)

relates: T-38 — that ticket proposes a networkSecurityConfig trusting
user-installed CAs (works in release; the "proper" self-host path) plus a
distinct SSLException error message. This ticket is the quicker debug-only
trust-all bypass. Complementary, not duplicate — coordinate so the two
cert-handling paths and their settings/error surfaces don't collide.

Done in 0bba163. Implemented exactly as specced: debug/release source-set split
(src/debug vs src/release DevCertTrust.kt) so the trust-all code is not compiled
into the release APK; BuildConfig.DEBUG-gated Settings toggle; persisted
ServerConfig.allowSelfSignedCerts default off; ApiProvider re-keys its client
cache on the flag so toggling takes effect without restart.

Security guarantee is VERIFIED by an automated release-variant test, not just by
inspection: testRelease/DevCertTrustReleaseTest does a real TLS handshake with
the flag ON against a self-signed MockWebServer and asserts it STILL throws
SSLHandshakeException (release no-op). testDebug/DevCertTrustDebugTest proves the
debug bypass connects (on) / rejects (off). Both variants' full unit suites +
lintDebug green.

Label was `human` (security review) — the release-exclusion mechanism is the
source-set split + the testRelease proof above; reviewer should sanity-check
those two files and that DevCertTrust is genuinely absent from any release
artifact. Note this required enabling buildConfig=true and adding okhttp-tls as
a testImplementation (fetched from Maven Central; offline builds needed one
online run to cache it).

Coordinated with T-38 as its note asked: T-38 remains the release-safe
networkSecurityConfig/user-CA path + distinct SSLException copy; this ticket is
the debug-only bypass. The two don't overlap.
